chicken-ns-as-to-part-baked-coated-skin-.title: Chicken, NS as part, baked, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. This product uses boneless breast or thigh meat, baked in the oven and coated with a crispy breading. The skin and coating are edible, adding flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken provides all essential amino acids required by the human body.
Baking retains more B‑vitamins compared to frying, where they can be lost.
The coating can be made from whole‑grain flour, breadcrumbs, or nut crumbs, increasing fiber content.
Chicken is one of the most affordable protein sources, making it accessible to many populations.
Various cultures season baked chicken with spices ranging from paprika to curry.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving of baked chicken provides about 25 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When baked without excessive oil, chicken remains low in fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken contains niacin (B3), B6, and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones, immunity, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: High protein and moderate fiber from the coating help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella or Campylobacter. Cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Allergy to coating ingredients
items.content: If the breading contains wheat, soy, or dairy, it can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared breadings often contain added salt. Choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Bread crumbs can raise blood sugar quickly, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked coated chicken can be served as a main dish, sliced for salads, sandwiches, or used in tacos. The skin and coating are eaten together, providing crunch and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consuming.

fruit-smoothie-juice-drink-no-dairy.title: Fruit Smoothie Juice Drink, No Dairy

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit smoothie juice drink, no dairy is a refreshing beverage made from fresh fruits, berries, water or plant‑based milk. It contains no dairy ingredients, making it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance. The smoothie is rich in vitamins, minerals and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoothies gained popularity in the United States in the 1970s as part of the health‑food movement.
Fiber content in smoothies is usually higher than in regular juices because whole fruits are blended.
Adding frozen berries creates a thick texture without the need for ice.
Combining different fruits enhances antioxidant bioavailability through synergistic effects.
Smoothies can be easily customized by swapping one fruit for another.

items.title: Rich in vitamins C and A
items.content: Fruits such as oranges, mangoes and berries provide vitamin C and provitamin A, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Water and plant‑based liquids in the smoothie help maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Whole fruits retain fiber, which promotes healthy digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Berries like blueberries and strawberries contain anthocyanins that combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The absence of dairy makes the drink virtually free of saturated fats, beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: A large amount of sweet fruits can raise the overall sugar level of the drink, which should be considered by people with diabetes.

items.title: Fruit allergies
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain fruits such as kiwi or strawberries.

items.title: Microbial contamination
items.content: Fresh produce must be thoroughly washed to avoid bacterial contamination in the smoothie.

items.title: Digestive issues with excess consumption
items.content: Large portions of smoothie may cause bloating due to high fruit sugar and fiber content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie immediately after blending, pour it over granola, use it as a base for protein shakes, or freeze into ice cubes for refreshing drinks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze individual portions in freezer‑safe bags.

sweet-potato-boiled-no-added-fat.title: Sweet potato, boiled, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato (batata) is a starchy root vegetable rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals. Boiling it without added fat retains most nutrients, gives a soft texture, and a mildly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potato belongs to the morning glory family, not the true potato family.
It contains more beta‑carotene than carrots, which converts to vitamin A during cooking.
In different regions it is called yam, camote, or batata.
It can be cultivated in tropical, subtropical, and even cooler climates with proper care.
Boiled sweet potato retains up to 90 % of its dietary fiber.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide steady energy and promote satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, supports gut microbiota, and can lower cholesterol.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6 and B5 are involved in protein and fat metabolism.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions can raise blood sugar quickly, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to sweet potato.

items.title: Watch for additives
items.content: If the sweet potato was pre‑processed, check for added preservatives that may be undesirable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled sweet potato can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, mashed, or used as a filling for pies. Cut into cubes for easy storage and reheating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled sweet potato in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions after cooling.
